html:
The Molasses Reef wreck is a small ship that sank on a reef in the Caicos Islands in the early 1500s, a few years after Columbus. It is the oldest European wreck in the Americas excavated by archaeologists.

Divers from Texas raised it in the 1980s. They found guns, anchors, tools and shackles, which suggest the crew may have been taking captives. Spanish ships of that time raided the islands for Lucayan people to work in the mines of Hispaniola.

No written record names the ship. Its finds are kept in the museum on Grand Turk and give a rare look at the first years of Spanish sailing in the region.
